Performers
Ferenc Fricsay (conductor), Berlin Symphonic Orchestra (orchestra, as credited) Documented

The English ensemble name is retained as Commons gives it. It has not been normalised to the Berlin Philharmonic or a particular incarnation of the Berlin radio orchestra.

[1]
Work version
Unknown Unknown

The performing edition and any editorial alterations are not identified in the recording sources.

[1]
Recorded
Unknown Disputed: sources disagree

The filename says November 1959, the description says November 1956, and embedded metadata labels 1954 as ‘Date and time of digitising’. That last tag is not established as either a session date or a genuine digitisation date. The 1928 date elsewhere on Commons concerns the composition.

  • November 1959 — filename attribution.
  • November 1956 — description attribution.
  • 1954 — unexplained embedded ‘Date and time of digitising’ tag; not a verified session date.

Transfer
Pablo Varela — audio restoration Documented

The embedded ‘Image title’ field explicitly says ‘Audio Restoration: Pablo Varela (2015)’. This does not identify the original recording engineer.

[2]
Transfer date
2015 Documented

Year attached to the named audio-restoration credit. It is distinct from the unexplained 1954 digitising tag and from the contested session years.

[2]
Processing
Audio restoration, credited to Pablo Varela; Ogg Vorbis encoding. Documented

The embedded credit does not identify equalisation, noise reduction, speed correction or other restoration operations. Encoder tags name Lavf56.36.100 and Lavc56.41.100 libvorbis.

[2]
Composition rights
Commons applies PD-old-70 to the composition. Documented

The tag concerns a copyright term measured from the composer’s death. It is not a recording licence, nor a worldwide determination of composition rights.

[1]
Recording rights
Rule 3 — territorial: sound recording public domain in the European Union (pre-1963 publication basis). Documented

Commons supplies only composition-level PD-old-70; its description says November 1956, its filename says November 1959, and the dossier preserves an unexplained 1954 embedded date. All three attributions precede 1963. The opened Fricsay/RIAS commercial-carrier listing also documents French 1955 and German 1958 editions, but has not been matched to this transfer and does not settle its session. Usable under the programme’s pre-1963 European sound-recording rule; the former 50-year term had expired before the 2013 extension. This is territorial, not a worldwide licence; US sound-recording status is not established. A recording date alone is not represented as an independently verified first-publication date.
